thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Slip Into Negative Territory as Trade Deal Hopes Dwindle

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Slip Into Negative Territory as Trade Deal Hopes Dwindle
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Friday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.3%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -1.03%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -0.3%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -1.7%
ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ): +5.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 1.7%.
US stocks were lower at session's half, reversing earlier gains after hopes for a US/China trade deal were dashed as economic adviser Larry Kudlow refuted a Bloomberg report that said President Donald Trump had requested a drafting of a U.S.-China trade accord. Trump tweeted on Thursday that he had a conversation with China President Xi Jinping that went well, saying the two had discussed trade. He said he's optimistic about a trade deal.
Meanwhile, Apple (AAPL) and Kraft Heinz (KHC) weighed on market sentiment after reporting their financial results. Apple logged losses as better-than-expected Q4 results were overshadowed by broadly flat shipments of its flagship product, the iPhone. On the other hand, Kraft Heinz posted earnings that missed market expectations as higher costs and lower pricing outweighed sluggish growth in net sales in Q3.
In economic data news, the US Labor Department Friday morning said payrolls rose by 250,000 last month, comfortably beating expectations of a 190,000 gain. The annual rate of wage growth reached 3.1%, its highest level since April 2009, as the tight labor market finally translated into higher income for employees.
The jobs data upstaged the swelling US trade deficit, now at $54 billion, as imports into the US reach a record high. And despite efforts by Washington, D.C. to curtail Chinese imports, the US trade deficit with China set another record high.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 2% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 2.1% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 2.2%.
VeriSign (VRSN) rose more than 15% after it reported Q3 revenue of $305.8 million, up 4.6% from $292.4 million in the year-ago quarter. Analysts polled by Capital IQ were expecting revenue of $305.48 million. Net income for the quarter ended Sept. 30 was $1.23 per share, compared with $1.00 per share in the year-ago period. Analysts were expecting EPS of $1.19.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 0.5%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 2.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 2.5%.
Synchrony Financial (SYF) fell nearly 10% following media reports that Walmart (WMT) sued the credit card issuer for allegedly breaching terms of its contract with the retailer. In the lawsuit filed in the US District Court of the Western District of Arkansas, Walmart claimed that Synchrony's underwriting standards have undermined its financial performance. Reports previously said that Walmart had complained to the consumer financial services company about rising loan losses, which resulted in less-than-expected revenue from the card partnership. The retailer said in the court filing that it is seeking damages "in an amount to be proven at trial but estimated to be no less than $800 million." Synchrony responded by saying that the lawsuit "is nothing more than an attempt by Walmart to exert leverage and avoid the contractually defined process for valuing the loan portfolio" that it has serviced on behalf of its customers. It also said that it intends to file substantial claims against the retailer to show how it improperly implemented the contract, including its mishandling of the card program both in stores and online.
Industrial
Select Sector SPDR-Industrial (XLI) was down 0.5% and other funds iShares Trust Dow Jones U.S. Industrial Sector Index Fund (IYJ), and Vanguard Industrials (VIS) were firmer.
Extreme Networks (EXTR) rose nearly 13% after it reported fiscal Q1 adjusted earnings of $0.08 per share compared with $0.16 per share in the year-ago period. The result was better than the consensus of $0.03 per share from analysts polled by CapIQ. Revenue came in at $239.9 million, which is up from $211.7 million a year ago and higher than the Street average of $233.4 million. For Q2, the company projects non-GAAP net income earnings in a range of $7.8 million to $15.4 million, or $0.06 to $0.13 per share. It expects revenue in a range of $239.0 million to $249.0 million. The company also said that the board has authorized the repurchase of up to $60 million of its common stock over the next two years. The repurchase will be funded using working capital.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 0.7% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.7%.
Parsley Energy (PE) rose more than 1% after it reported late Thursday Q3 adjusted earnings of $0.45 per share, up from $0.39 per share a year earlier and higher than the $0.44 per share Street consensus estimate compiled by Capital IQ.Total revenue for the quarter was $511 million, up from $241 million reported for the same period last year and higher than the $493 million Street estimate.
Commodities
Crude was down 0.9%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 0.9%. Natural gas was up 1.4% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 1.1%.
Gold was down 0.5%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.1%. Silver was down 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.7% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 0.1%.
Puma Biotechnology (PBYI) plummeted 49% to the lowest level since May 2016 after the company reported better-than-expected results for Q3, but said sales of its early stage breast cancer treatment, Nerlynx, increased by just 3.5% from last quarter. Sales increased to $62.6 million from $6.1 million a year ago, beating the Capital IQ consensus estimate of $57.9 million. Adjusted net income increased to $0.16 per share compared from a loss of $1.36 per share a year ago and beat estimates for a loss of $0.45 per share. On an unadjusted basis, the company lost $0.36 per share versus a loss of $2.07 last year.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.9% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were weaker.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.03% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were lower.
Newell Brands (NWL) surged more than 14% after reporting normalized diluted EPS from continuing operations of $0.54 for Q3, in line compared to the prior year but below the Capital IQ consensus of $0.64. Net sales dropped to $2.28 billion from $2.47 billion while analysts polled by Capital IQ were looking for $2.34 billion. For 2018, the company raised its normalized diluted EPS guidance range to $2.55 - $2.75 from $2.45 - $2.65, while keeping its net sales target within the range of $8.7 billion - $9 billion. Analysts are expecting FY18 EPS of $2.47 and sales of $9.05 billion.
